lesson.title: Four ways to undo a step
lesson.skill: Choose which inverse operation to use, and know what each one costs.
lesson.missionLink: You keep undoing the same step in the same way and then losing track. This is the whole set on one screen.

primarySource.why: It tabulates the four moves and their failure modes.

content.text: Every step you undo has a cost. Read across a row before you commit to it.

rows: Work backwards
Start from the answer and undo the operations in reverse order.
You have to know the answer, which is the thing you are trying to find.
You find yourself writing the answer before you have earned it.
Isolate the term
Move everything that is not the term to the other side, one operation at a time.
The term appears twice, so there is nothing to isolate.
You subtract a letter from both sides and the letter survives.
Balance both sides
Apply the same operation to both sides and the equality holds.
The operation changes what one side means, such as squaring a side that may be negative.
The two sides stop being the same kind of thing.
Guess and check
Try a number, see what comes out, and adjust from there.
The step is slow, and a learner doing forty of them feels every one.
You find yourself trying the same number twice in a row.
Graph it
Plot both sides and look for where they cross.
The crossing is between two whole numbers and the graph is too coarse to show it.
Your plotted points are two and your answer is two and a half.
